A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Franca and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Content can be matched reliably across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original Franca experiments on classification, segmentation, robustness, and 3D understanding, together with component and RASA ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds register-token experiments, token-norm analysis, PCA compression results, and expanded controlled comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same Matryoshka clustering, CyclicMask, and RASA procedures and objectives. Adding registers is tested as an ablation; the proposed Franca architecture remains register-free.

E1.justification: The training datasets and classification, segmentation, robustness, OOD, and 3D task coverage are retained. The new register and compression analyses reuse existing datasets, principally ImageNet-1K and ADE20K, without introducing a distinct population or task.

E2.justification: v4 Table 2 adds DINOv2 explicitly augmented with HRFT and RASA to the controlled classification and dense-prediction comparison; v3 Figure 2b has no corresponding arm. The named baseline families otherwise remain unchanged. DINOv2-R was already evaluated in v3.

E3.justification: The controlled comparison changes from v3's stated no-HRFT setup to explicit with/without HRFT+RASA conditions in v4 Table 2. New appendix experiments test registers and ImageNet-1K linear probing after PCA truncation to 200, 100, 50, 25, and 10 components. Existing implementation and evaluation settings in Appendices B–C remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds tests of whether registers help Franca and compares layer-wise maximum token norms. Appendix D.4 tests feature compression after PCA, extending the existing raw-feature slicing analysis. The controlled comparison is revised, while the component ablation and all existing RASA sensitivity sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs for Feat2GS, five seeds for overclustering and in-context segmentation, and seed 42 for the qualitative image selection. The additions introduce no new run-count disclosure, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The controlled result set is revised: v3 Figure 2b lists Franca-B KNN/IN-val as 79.5/82.6, whereas v4 Table 2 separates 77.5/82.0 without HRFT+RASA from 79.6/82.6 with it. Newly reported register experiments show 79.6 to 78.7 KNN and 46.2 to 45.5 ADE20K segmentation; Table 9 adds PCA results, including 22.8 versus 37.2 at 50 components for DINOv2-L versus Franca-L. Main benchmark tables otherwise retain their scores.

T1.justification: The nested-subspace definitions, summed clustering loss, and RASA projection derivation, including Equations 1–3, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, propositions, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of a fully open vision foundation model, Matryoshka clustering and positional disentanglement innovations, and strong performance without large-model distillation. The added experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix D.1 attributes suppression of high-norm artifacts to nested clustering, argues that registers are redundant and harmful for Franca, and explains the primary baseline choice. D.4 interprets PCA compression results as evidence of preserved semantic structure. Section 3.1 shifts its emphasis from robustness gains toward dense prediction.

D1.justification: The new analyses specify PCA-before-truncation and retained dimensions, plus the backbone, pretraining datasets, and validation data used for token-norm measurements. Core hyperparameters, hardware, and access information remain unchanged. Computational-cost details move from Section 3.5/Table 5 to Appendix D.3/Table 8 without numerical revision.

R1.justification: The same 93 references, Appendix A discussion, and positioning relative to concurrent DINOv3 are retained. Franca's favorable comparison with register-based DINOv2 already appears in v3; the new discussion supplies additional mechanism arguments and evidence.

P1.justification: v4 adds two focused appendix subsections, moves computational cost into the appendix, and makes local prose and cross-reference edits. The author affiliation changes from Valeo.ai to Qualcomm AI Research with a work-location footnote. The main narrative and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The radar comparison in Figure 2b is replaced by Table 2, while Figure 2a becomes a standalone figure. v4 adds the token-norm Figure 10 and PCA Table 9, relocates the computational-cost table and attention visualization, and repacks the final ablation tables. Most existing visual content and the two-column design are preserved.

improvement.justification: The explicit HRFT+RASA controls in Table 2 and new register and PCA analyses provide useful additional checks of existing design choices. Main benchmarks and the full RASA sweeps remain available. The gain is limited by the narrower controlled-comparison task summary and reporting inconsistencies, including 22.0 in Appendix D.4 versus 22.8 in Table 9, but the added experimental support yields a modest overall improvement.
